city_center.name: Downtown Las Vegas / Downtown Summerlin
city_center.landmark: the Mojave Desert valley ringed by the Spring Mountains and Red Rock Canyon to the west, Lake Mead to the southeast; Downtown Summerlin is the suburban farmers-market anchor
city_center.notes: Las Vegas sits in a Mojave Desert basin between Red Rock Canyon and Lake Mead; the Las Vegas Farmers Market at Downtown Summerlin (The Pavilion, Sat) is the most accessible market, bringing Southwest produce to the valley. sources: st-aug.edu Las Vegas Mojave/Lake Mead geography; fabulousnevada.com Las Vegas farmers markets; britannica.com Las Vegas.

featured_frontier.photo_cue: melon + dates, cast iron, Summerlin market pavilion, Red Rock Canyon red sandstone west
featured_frontier.signature_ingredient: Southwest desert melons + dates + citrus (Mojave-valley market produce)

audience: Mojave-valley families, large-household and service-industry base, fast-growing metro; Smith's + Albertsons + Costco + Walmart shoppers, 24-hour desert city

cultural_notes: Las Vegas sits at the crossroads of the Mojave Desert to the north and west and the Lake Mead National Recreation Area to the southeast; Red Rock Canyon's red sandstone escarpment rises just west of the valley (source: st-aug.edu where in America is Las Vegas; britannica.com Las Vegas outdoor recreation)

beyond the Strip, the valley has a real farmers-market and farm-to-table movement -- the Las Vegas Farmers Market at Downtown Summerlin brings the freshest Southwest fruits and vegetables to the community (source: fabulousnevada.com 5 Las Vegas farmers markets; lasvegasweekly.com farm to table)

Las Vegas is a large, fast-growing, 24-hour service-economy metro with a substantial Filipino and Hispanic workforce shaping the food culture (INFERRED demographic framing -- verify tone before production)
the desert setting means most fresh produce is imported; Red Rock Canyon and Lake Mead are the genuine wild-land recreation anchors (source: britannica.com Las Vegas; st-aug.edu)
